hooks.text: A giant human skull once flew past Earth on Halloween night.
Why did a giant skull-shaped rock fly past Earth on Halloween?
A 2,000-foot-wide skull missed Earth by only 300,000 miles.

title: The Halloween Skull Asteroid
description: On Halloween 2015, a 2,000-foot-wide dead comet shaped like a human skull zipped past Earth.

beats.text: A giant human skull once flew past Earth on Halloween night.
beats.visual: Arecibo Observatory radar image of 2015 TB145 showing the skull feature, 2015

beats.text: On October 10, 2015, astronomers in Hawaii spotted a massive object inbound.
beats.visual: Pan-STARRS telescope on Haleakala, Maui, Hawaii, 2015

beats.text: It was moving at 78,000 miles per hour, closing the gap in three weeks.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the orbital path of near-Earth object 2015 TB145 relative to Earth, 2015

beats.text: On Halloween day, it missed us by only 300,000 miles, just beyond the Moon.
beats.visual: Diagram of the Earth and Moon showing the distance of the 2015 TB145 flyby, 2015

beats.text: Scientists at the Arecibo Observatory bounced radar off the surface to reveal its shape.
beats.visual: Arecibo Observatory radio telescope dish in Puerto Rico, 2015
queries: Arecibo Observatory radio telescope Puerto Rico

beats.text: The returning image showed two hollow eye sockets and a nose above a chin.
beats.visual: Close-up radar imaging of 2015 TB145 revealing a skull-like appearance, 2015

beats.text: Astronomers discovered it was a dead comet, not an asteroid.
beats.visual: Artist concept of an extinct dead comet drifting through deep space

beats.text: This 2,000-foot corpse reflects light like dark asphalt.
beats.visual: A dark asteroid surface comparable to the color of fresh black asphalt
